question: How Do I Add a Custom Order Status to WooCommerce?
metaDescription: Registering a new status is a small code snippet, but the real work is deciding which core behaviors (emails, stock, reports) should react to it.
shortAnswer: Registering a new order status is a fairly small code snippet using register_post_status() and a filter to add it to the order status list — the more substantial work is deciding how the rest of the system should treat it: does it trigger any emails, does it count toward sales reports, does it affect stock, and where does it fit relative to the existing statuses in the fulfillment sequence.

bodyHtml:
How to Register a Custom Status

A custom order status is registered as a WordPress post status, then added to WooCommerce's known list of order statuses via a filter so it appears correctly in the admin order screen's status dropdown and reporting logic.

add_action( 'init', function() {
    register_post_status( 'wc-awaiting-approval', [
        'label' => 'Awaiting Approval',
        'public' => true,
        'exclude_from_search' => false,
        'show_in_admin_all_list' => true,
        'show_in_admin_status_list' => true,
        'label_count' => _n_noop( 'Awaiting Approval (%s)', 'Awaiting Approval (%s)' ),
    ] );
} );

add_filter( 'wc_order_statuses', function( $statuses ) {
    $statuses['wc-awaiting-approval'] = 'Awaiting Approval';
    return $statuses;
} );

The Harder Design Decisions

  • Where the new status fits in the existing sequence — does it come before Processing, replace part of it, or sit alongside existing statuses for a specific workflow branch?
  • Whether it should trigger customer or admin emails, which needs its own explicit email template and trigger hook, since a custom status has no automatic email tied to it by default.
  • Whether it should count toward sales reports and analytics, which needs explicit inclusion since WooCommerce's default reporting logic only recognizes its own built-in statuses.
  • How stock behaves at this status — should it reduce, hold, or remain untouched, which needs to align with the store's actual fulfillment logic.

Implementing It Properly

  1. Register the status and add it to the order statuses filter as shown above.
  2. Map out exactly how emails, stock, and reporting should behave at this status before writing that supporting logic.
  3. Test the full order lifecycle including transitions into and out of the new status.
